title: Chapter 26: The Third Choice
content:
Chapter 26:

A Third Option

Running frantically, he didn’t know how much time had passed.

His breath ran out, his knees buckled, dripping sweat ran down his chin; with the inside of his heart a mess, he still continued to run without being able to stop.

If he didn’t run, he would be caught up by the incomprehensible emotions chasing him from behind. And if he were caught by them, this time everything would surely end—that conviction alone was now driving Subaru.

Ram’s scream, her roar of resentment, that cry that regarded Subaru as an object of hatred, still wouldn’t leave his ears.

Ram, who never broke her rude, haughty attitude that seemed to mock people.

That same Ram had bared such emotion and screamed hatred at the top of her voice.

Just recalling it made his heart shrink, and indescribable sadness came and went.

He had run away. He had ended up running away.

Rushing through, bursting out of the mansion, throwing away all the noise heard from behind, he had run away leaving everything behind.

Subaru could no longer return to that place.

Ram and Roswaal wouldn’t forgive the Subaru who ran, and Emilia and Puck likely wouldn’t be able to fully trust the Subaru who stubbornly kept his mouth shut.

And Beatrice, who was bound by contract, also likely wouldn’t become an active ally without being able to read the true intent of Subaru’s actions.

If he could have spilled everything, that would have been fine too.

But to do that, the black mist stood in his way and interfered.

In a world where time had stopped, in a world where sound was isolated, pain like his heart being crushed and fear—before that, Subaru’s wavering resolve was easily blown away.

As a result, unable to endure either the pain or the sorrow, Subaru had no choice but to run.

“It can’t be helped, can it…! What could I… Even I!”

He didn’t understand anything.

Why it had turned out like this, what he had to do.

What he had to do for the world to forgive Subaru.

“Even though… it was… so fun…”

Suddenly invited into another world, having no choice but to live in a world where he knew nothing; a place that welcomed Subaru in a world where only that anxiety was rooted.

Those days, that time, that time where only about a single week had passed, was now so far away it was out of the current Subaru’s reach.

Redoing, returning, repeating; each time, the world bared its fangs at Subaru.

The world that had been so kind changed color, the brilliance that had been vivid faded, and everything looked dull.

—It’s no good anymore.

Suddenly, such a mutter grazed his mind.

—There’s no need to try hard anymore, is there?

At his own voice urging resignation, at that sweet temptation, Subaru almost stopped thinking.

If he did just as those words said, he thought he would surely be at ease.

Originally, Subaru had a nature of easily drifting toward the easier, easier direction of the situation.

It wasn’t just Subaru. Any human would likely be the same.

If two choices were lined up in front of them, and they couldn’t throw away either, they would be forced into a time of anguish.

In the midst of struggling with such suffering, what if a third option were suddenly presented?

If that option seemed attractive, as if it were a divine revelation, as if it were a godsend, who could blame the impulse to reach out for it?

If one could choose neither to resist nor to escape completely, wouldn’t it be better to just throw it all away?

“Throw it away… you say.”

Blood rapidly drained from his head, and even the pounding of his heart, which had been beating so fast, felt like something distant.

His limbs became heavily weighted, and his legs, which had been moving as if driven, slowed their pace, gradually changing to a dragging walk.

Suddenly, his field of vision, which had become invisible until then, expanded, and Subaru realized his figure was in a forest surrounded by trees.

While running recklessly, he seemed to have burst out of the mansion, gone off the highway, and wandered into a mountain path.

Surrounded by dense, overgrown greenery, in the gloom where even the sky was blocked, Subaru thought that this place resembled the place of his previous death.

The moment he thought that, a clear vision of the third option floated up.

“If I die…”

Would I be saved, from this situation?

“Ah, that’s right. If I end up dying, it changes.”

The nonsense born of weakness that slipped out of his mouth seemed too sweet, and a twitching smile floated onto Subaru’s lips.

Subaru had already lost his life three times.

A fourth death was inexperienced for Subaru. Therefore, he had been tormented by the baseless anxiety that if he met a fourth death, perhaps everything would end.

But,

“If it ends with that, what’s wrong with it…?”

Each time he repeated, the situation Subaru was placed in got worse.

Death by debilitation, beaten to death after being debilitated. Murdered by a person he should have trusted, and this time the death of that partner, and the loss of all trust from the other concerned parties.

This time, where he picked up only his life. This time, where he was made to hold nothing but his life.

Like this, losing everything, continuing to struggle under conditions worse than when he was first invited to the parallel world. What meaning would there be in such a thing?

No, even if there were some meaning, why was it said that Subaru had to walk it?

“If you want to do it, you should just do it on your own… What relationship does it have with me, with 

me

?”

Biting his lip, he spat hatred at the existence that involved him in this situation.

Muddy dark emotions boiled in his guts, curses as far as he could think of filled his head, pouring black fuel into Subaru’s heart, which had already completely withered.

—The choice called “Death,” it seemed like the best idea to the current Subaru.

If it ends by dying, then that’s that.

But if, hypothetically, he could die and return to the “Second Day” again.

“The first… that’s right. Getting along with Emilia-tan, fluffing Puck, teasing Beatrice, exchanging banter with Roswaal, together with Ram and Rem…”

Tracing the first time just as it was, he might be able to do it happily.

Come to think of it, the first time could be said to be the ideal itself for Subaru. Even if the future of dying from debilitation at the end on the night of the fourth day couldn’t be changed, that death was accompanied by neither pain nor suffering, and above all, peace and tranquility were promised.

If he could return to those days again, if he could come in contact with their smiles, then dying was by no means a scary thing.

The current situation, which was beyond help, was far more terrifying for Subaru, and above all, he couldn’t endure the sadness.

Swallowing his breath, Subaru searched the pocket of his trousers.

Inside, the thin sensation he grasped in his hand was the quill pen he hadn’t let go of even once in these four days.

The sharp pen tip had pierced the back of Subaru’s hand countless times, stained with fresh blood each time, and the now dark red, caked-on blood likely couldn’t be wiped off even if he tried.

Gripping the quill pen in a reverse hold, Subaru pointed its tip at his own throat.

The pointed tip possessed sharpness sufficient to gouge the human body; that was something Subaru himself could already testify to with his own body.

If he gathered momentum and swung it down with all his might, the objective would likely be achieved.

“Haa… haa… haa… gh.”

His vision flickered on and off, and his whole body was hot as if boiling from the too-rapid blood circulation.

And yet blood didn’t circulate only to his head, and the spinning of his brain froze more and more as if it knew no limits.

His gaze staring at the pen tip was fixed, and the trembling tip approached inch by inch.

His rough breathing, surpassing even a full sprint, was accompanied by nausea, to the extent that if his concentration broke, he seemed likely to vomit stomach acid immediately.

His knees shook, his lower back gave way, and his arm didn’t move as if nerves didn’t pass beyond the elbow. Yet only his right hand gripping the pen was trembling ridiculously, comically.

“Damn… it.”

Clicking his tongue, he shook his head as if to deceive the emotions before his eyes.

He grabbed and fixed his trembling right wrist with his left hand. But the moment he touched his right hand, the fear was transmitted to his left hand as well. Both hands gripping the pen trembled minutely, and that intent was never carried out.

“Stop… I said 

stop

!”

He raised his voice in irritation, but even that voice couldn’t fully hide the trembling.

Finally, he dropped the quill pen he was holding, and when he bent his back to pick it up, his knees, which should have been buckling, lost their strength and he collapsed on the spot.

Putting both hands on the soil, staring at the ground close up in astonishment, Subaru suddenly spilled hot things welling up from both eyes, and bit through his lip in frustration.

Sharp pain and the iron smell of blood filled his mouth, and tasting that, he sobbed.

“I can’t even… even such a simple thing…”

—Is it that I lack courage and can’t do it?

If he tumbled down there, he could be at ease.

Despite brooding like that, Subaru couldn’t even determine the resolve to fall completely.

He couldn’t lose to impulse and leave it to momentum, nor could he put an easy and weak decision into action. Even his determination and resolve were fragile; crouching and wailing was the most he could do.

Even if he exposed such a shameful state, the situation wouldn’t improve one bit. It wouldn’t even worsen. Change would not occur. The unchanging situation just simply conveyed that the current state Subaru was placed in was rock bottom.

Pain, suffering, sadness; everything pressing Subaru for a decision, absolutely everything, granted him no kindness.

Even the option he had craved so much, he didn’t have the resolve to carry it out.

He thought that if he was going to choose the end anyway, maybe it would have been better to let Ram kill him.

Subaru was not directly related to Rem’s cause of death. Therefore, even if Ram could have killed Subaru, it would have been nothing but a completely misplaced revenge play.

Ram, who wailed at the intense pain of having half her body torn away, and screamed hatred so much.

If it could soothe that body-scorching impulse even a little, wouldn’t it be fine to offer up something like the life of Subaru, who had chosen only to rot away like this?

While seeming to care for others, its essence was escapism just to distract from the whereabouts of his own unsettled resolve.

However, Subaru, who avoided even facing his own shame, never realized that thought which insulted even Ram who was being used as a comparison.

That selfish emotion that even spirits would abandon—what dispatched that there was, perhaps, the dispensation of heaven unable to bear seeing such a shameful sight.

“——Ah?”

At the sensation of the air suddenly changing, Subaru, who was groveling, raised his face.

On the soil where he crouched, there was no change in his vision crumpled by tears. But in the gloom where sunlight didn’t penetrate, blocked by leaves and branches, something caught on Subaru’s nerves.

It was a warning called up from instinct.

Raising his body at the ringing alarm bells, Subaru looked around while kneeling on one knee. Rubbing his eyes, securing his vision, straining his ears, and killing his breath.

The sound of grass being stepped on rang out, and the dry echoes of swaying branches followed in succession.

Fast. And sharp. Something was closing in sharply and rapidly.

Unknowingly moistening his dry lips with his tongue, Subaru instantly picked up the quill pen that had fallen at his feet. Holding it in a reverse grip, he held it in front of him with anxiety whose reason he didn’t understand.

—In an instant, it pushed aside the vegetation and revealed itself before Subaru.

“Y-You are…”

A pursuer from the mansion—it was not.

Or perhaps the weakness that somewhere hoped if it were was betrayed.

Before his eyes, which he cast down slightly at the selfish expectation, however, it stood leisurely.

Speaking from Subaru’s knowledge, it was likely closest to a wolf.

Its whole body was covered in black fur, its four legs firmly biting the soil, keeping its body low. Saliva dripped from a large mouth lined with sharp fangs, and in the center of a face covered in jet black, red twin eyes, the only things asserting their presence, shone brilliantly.

Its body length was roughly about one meter, and its weight was probably about thirty or forty kilos.

In his original world, it would be the size of a large dog class, but from its overall sharp body shape, he didn’t feel that much overwhelming strength.

However,

“Hey, hey…”

In front of that existence with glaring eyes before its prey, breathing roughly, could a human who knew only the lukewarm dogs blended into human society maintain composure?

Before that thing shaking its fangs with obvious hostility, cold sweat rapidly wet Subaru’s forehead.

In front of Subaru, who couldn’t make a single move, it lowered its head and snorted.

Likely, it had sniffed out Subaru’s scent and come this far. Subaru’s body, which had run recklessly, had many abrasions from grazing branches, and there were not a few places still oozing blood. On top of that, he had even been raising unsightly sobs. It wouldn’t have lacked materials to pinpoint his location.

The black dog lowering its head and threatening him.

Suddenly, he saw a yellowish horn growing on the top of that dog’s head, proving that its ecology was definitely different from what Subaru knew.

At the ferocious rage of the horned beast hungry for food, Subaru felt his courage shrink, but on the other hand, realized he was obtaining even a sense of relief from unknown origins.

Perhaps if it was the beast before his eyes, it would affirm Subaru’s decision without hesitation. Because to the cornered Subaru, it seemed like such an existence.

“Thinking I’d let Ram kill me… and right after that, this. Even I think I’m too fickle.”

Because he couldn’t hold a firm resolve, he continued to be swept away by the situation before his eyes.

Just as it had been until now, even now he ended up entrusting himself to the easy situation before his eyes.

He didn’t think making that choice was a mistake. Even if he thought so, it was useless, and even if he thought so, nothing would change.

Spreading both arms, Subaru expressed non-resistance to the horned existence.

For an instant, perhaps unable to understand the meaning of the prey’s action, the horned beast keeping its body low trembled as if frightened, which was a little funny.

“Wh-at are you scared of, against a guy beaten down this much?”

A laugh that slipped out of his mouth.

He was amazed that he still had the energy left to laugh like that.

—He felt somewhat at ease, enough that laughter came out.

The black beast standing in his way—this guy, who clearly regarded Subaru as prey, was the messenger of heaven who would grant Subaru’s wish.

It would likely guide Subaru, who couldn’t even end his own life, to a gentle and sweet stagnation with those fangs, those claws, and that horn.

Whether it would end in death, or return and sink into lazy happiness.

He didn’t know which would be thrust upon him, but he could escape from this helpless dead end pressing on Subaru.

For now, that was fine. Just that was fine. He wouldn’t wish for any luxury beyond that.

So rather, put me out of my misery—

“Huh…?”

Even though he should have been thinking that with a clear feeling, cold water was thrown on Subaru’s mood by the sound of hard things clattering close by.

Surroundings; while paying attention to the threat before his eyes, he searched for the cause of the sound, but it wasn’t found anywhere visible.

And so he realized immediately. No wonder it wasn’t found. It was natural.

The small, hard sound was the sound of the roots of Subaru’s teeth trembling, unable to mesh.

“——Eh?”

The lips leaking a mutter trembled, blood flow concentrated in his fingers to the point of pain, and it was ringing at a speed that could make Subaru’s heart explode.

The abnormality occurring in his own body; noticing it belatedly, Subaru was astonished.

Why did his body want to escape from this place so much?

Like this, it was as if—

“This is just like…”

—Like I don’t want to die, isn’t it?

His heart betrayed even by his body, Subaru was distressed by the situation where he could no longer trust even his own self. And, ignoring Subaru’s disturbed emotions,

“Oah…?”

The beast suddenly vanished from his field of vision, and a stupid voice dropped into the forest.

Dumbfounded, he chased the whereabouts of the jet-black shadow that had been there just a moment ago. Not found.

Immediately after, the base of his right leg was bitten into by powerful jaws.

“Ggh…!”

Fangs pierced flesh, reached nerves, and the wound was widened by sharpness like a blade.

Blood spurted, the movement of the world became slow, and looking down in a daze at the source of the pain, Subaru’s eyes crossed with the red twin eyes thrusting fangs into there.

—As if loudly asserting that he was alive, Subaru’s scream echoed throughout the forest.
